ColonyCouncil.EncounterDef.label: a still morning on the lake

texts.li: Mist lay on the lake this morning, and {A_nameDef} watched {X_indefinite} wade out of it to drink, rings spreading across the still water.
{A_nameDef} went down to the lake with a bucket and found {X_indefinite} already there, drinking, not much bothered by company.
[cold] A skin of ice had formed at the lake's edge overnight, and {X_definite} broke through it to drink. {A_nameDef} heard the crack from the path.
[child] {A_nameDef} was skipping stones across the lake until {X_indefinite} came down to drink, and then sat very still to watch it instead.
Out on the frozen lake, {X_indefinite} picked its way across the ice, testing every step. {A_nameDef} watched from the shore, and went the long way round.
{A_nameDef} heard the lake ice groan in the cold and looked up to see {X_indefinite} stop dead in the middle of it, then carry on, slower.
[snow] Snow drifted over the frozen lake, and {X_indefinite} left a line of tracks straight across it that {A_nameDef} didn't trust enough to follow.
{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} showed {A_nameDef} how their people set night lines along a lake shore: a stick, a length of cord, and patience until morning.
Where the reeds thin out is where the fish lie in the heat, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, pointing across the lake with a crust of bread.
[theirLowtech] While they talked by the lake, {X_nameDef} wove {A_nameDef} a fish trap from willow, quick as knitting, and left it as a gift.
[winter] {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} how {FACTION} people cut holes in lake ice and fish through them, and how many toes that has cost over the years.
Watch where the water breaks white over the stones, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} at the river: that's where it's shallow enough to cross.
{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} walked {A_nameDef} down to the river and showed {A_objective} the ford their traders use, marked by a split boulder on the far bank.
[rain] The river was up after the rain. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} to give it a day before crossing, however shallow it looked.
[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} showed {A_nameDef} how to cross a river with a pole held upstream, leaning on the water instead of fighting it.

ColonyCouncil.EncounterDef.label: at the river at first light

texts.li: At first light {A_nameDef} found {X_indefinite} drinking at the river, mist rising off the water round its legs.
Down at the river, {A_nameDef} and {X_indefinite} drank a few yards apart, each keeping half an eye on the other.
[child] {A_nameDef} went to the river to fill a jug and came back without it, having followed {X_indefinite} along the bank instead.
The river ran high and brown after the rain. {A_nameDef} watched {X_indefinite} pace the far bank for a long time before it waded in, and let out a breath when it climbed out on this side.
Swollen with rain, the river had cut off a strip of the far bank with {X_indefinite} stranded on it. By evening the water had dropped, and {A_nameDef} saw it pick its way home.
[storm] Lightning over the hills, and the river rising. On the far bank {X_indefinite} turned and turned, waiting, while {A_nameDef} hauled the last of the washing in from the water's edge.

ColonyCouncil.EncounterDef.label: the tide line after a storm

texts.li: After the night's storm the tide line was thick with weed and broken wood. {A_nameDef} gathered driftwood while {X_indefinite} picked through the wrack further along for whatever the sea had left.
{A_nameDef} walked the beach at low tide, turning over driftwood, and kept finding {X_indefinite} a little way ahead, turning over the same things for different reasons.
[cold] Frost on the sand, and the sea gray and flat. {A_nameDef} found {X_indefinite} nosing along the tide line and shared the beach with it for the morning.
{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} showed {A_nameDef} a knot coast people use for mooring, one that holds under any load and comes loose with a single tug.
Sitting on the sea wall, {X_nameDef} mended a net and talked {A_nameDef} through every knot of it, until {A_nameDef} could do a row alone.
[theirLowtech] Seaweed dried on the rocks makes a winter soup, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, and {FACTION} children are raised on it.
[storm] {X_nameDef} could read the weather off the color of the sea, and told {A_nameDef} so an hour before the storm proved it.
{A_nameDef} crouched over a rock pool at low tide and found {X_indefinite} doing much the same on the far side of it.
[child] {A_nameDef} spent the afternoon at the rock pools with {X_indefinite} for company, poking at everything that moved and some things that didn't.
[child] {A_nameDef} came back from the rocks soaked to the knees, with a pocketful of shells and a long story about {X_indefinite}.

plain.li: [morning] Mist on the water at first light, and something drinking in it. I stood there until my feet were wet.
[winter] The lake is frozen from bank to bank. An animal crossed it today; I didn't.
[rain] The river came up in the night and took the bank with it. It'll go down. It always does.
A traveler showed me the ford today. I've crossed that river the hard way for a year.

cheerful.li: Learned to set a night line from a traveler. Tomorrow we find out if there's a fish on it!

plain.li: Driftwood all along the tide line after the storm. I brought back an armful and a sore back.
Spent an hour at the rock pools. Small things live in there that I didn't know about.
A traveler taught me a mooring knot. I've tied it to everything since, the door included.

gloomy.li: The sea washed up planks from a boat today. I hope whoever was in it got home.
